knowledge:
- key_parameters: cutoff=Threshold on the variation coefficient to filter out low-varying features in remove.low.cv ;; ncomp=Number of components to define clusters, optimized via getNcomp ;; keepX/keepY=Number of features to keep per component to define a cluster signature, optimized via tuneCluster functions ;; scale/center=Logicals in pca, pls, and plotLong to scale or center time profiles ;; mode=Character string indicating the multi-block PLS mode (e.g., "canonical")
- alternatives: lmms::lmmSpline=Used for modeling time-course data by taking into account inter-individual variability ;; lmms::lmmsDE=Used for statistical testing of profiles that are not differentially expressed over time ;; mixOmics=The underlying package providing multivariate ordination methods (PCA, PLS, block PLS)
- when_to_use: Use this framework when you have longitudinal multi-omics datasets (e.g., transcriptomics, metabolomics, microbiome) measured on the same biological samples across multiple time points, and you want to identify co-expressed temporal feature signatures.
- pitfalls: Straight line modeling can occur when inter-individual variation is too high, requiring filtering with lmms.filter.lines ;; Interpretation based on raw correlations between profiles can be spurious, so proportionality distance (proportionality function) should be used for post-hoc validation ;; The lmms package is archived on CRAN and must be installed from GitHub (cran/lmms)

workflows.name: single_omic_longitudinal_clustering
workflows.intent: Model and cluster longitudinal features from a single omics dataset to find groups of features with similar temporal profiles.
input: sim.data (matrix or data.frame of expression/abundance values with samples in rows and features in columns)
time (numeric vector containing sample time point information)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter low-variation features using a coefficient of variation threshold ;; 2. Model features as a function of time using linear mixed model splines ;; 3. Filter out noisy or straight-line profiles ;; 4. Perform PCA and optimize the number of components ;; 5. Extract clusters and plot longitudinal profiles ;; 6. Optimize feature selection using sparse PCA to identify a cluster signature
workflows.code:
data("timeOmics.simdata")
sim.data <- timeOmics.simdata$sim

remove.low.cv <- function(X, cutoff = 0.5){
  # var.coef
  cv <- unlist(lapply(as.data.frame(X), 
                      function(x) abs(sd(x)/mean(x))))
  return(X[,cv > cutoff])
}

data.filtered <- remove.low.cv(sim.data, 0.5)
time <- timeOmics.simdata$time
lmms.output <- timeOmics.simdata$lmms.output
modelled.data <- timeOmics.simdata$modelled
filter.res <- lmms.filter.lines(data = data.filtered, 
                                lmms.obj = lmms.output, time = time)
profile.filtered <- filter.res$filtered
pca.res <- pca(X = profile.filtered, ncomp = 5, scale=FALSE, center=FALSE)
pca.ncomp <- getNcomp(pca.res, max.ncomp = 5, X = profile.filtered, 
                      scale = FALSE, center=FALSE)
pca.res <- pca(X = profile.filtered, ncomp = 2, scale = FALSE, center=FALSE)
pca.cluster <- getCluster(pca.res)
plotIndiv(pca.res)
plotVar(pca.res)
plotLoadings(pca.res)
plotLong(pca.res, scale = FALSE, center = FALSE, 
         title = "PCA longitudinal clustering")
tune.spca.res <- tuneCluster.spca(X = profile.filtered, ncomp = 2, 
                                  test.keepX = c(2:10))
spca.res <- spca(X = profile.filtered, ncomp = 2, 
                 keepX = tune.spca.res$choice.keepX, scale = FALSE)
plotLong(spca.res)

workflows.name: multi_omic_two_blocks_clustering
workflows.intent: Integrate and cluster longitudinal features from two different omics datasets to find common temporal profiles and signatures.
input: profile.filtered (modeled and filtered matrix of the first omic block)
timeOmics.simdata$Y (matrix of the second omic block with matching samples/rows)
workflows.stages: 1. Perform PLS and optimize the number of components ;; 2. Extract clusters and plot longitudinal profiles ;; 3. Optimize feature selection for both blocks using sparse PLS to identify a joint signature
workflows.code:
X <- profile.filtered
Y <- timeOmics.simdata$Y

pls.res <- pls(X,Y, ncomp = 5, scale = FALSE)
pls.ncomp <- getNcomp(pls.res, max.ncomp = 5, X=X, Y=Y, scale = FALSE)
pls.res <- pls(X,Y, ncomp = 2, scale = FALSE)
head(getCluster(pls.res))
plotLong(pls.res, title = "PLS longitudinal clustering", legend = TRUE)
tune.spls <- tuneCluster.spls(X, Y, ncomp = 2, test.keepX = c(4:10), test.keepY <- c(2,4,6))
spls.res <- spls(X,Y, ncomp = 2, scale = FALSE, 
                 keepX = tune.spls$choice.keepX, keepY = tune.spls$choice.keepY)
spls.cluster <- getCluster(spls.res)
plotLong(spls.res, title = "sPLS clustering")

workflows.name: multi_block_omics_clustering
workflows.intent: Integrate and cluster longitudinal features from three or more omics datasets, identify signatures, and perform post-hoc validation.
input: profile.filtered (modeled and filtered matrix of the first omic block)
timeOmics.simdata$Z (matrix of the third omic block)
timeOmics.simdata$Y (matrix of the second omic block)
workflows.stages: 1. Perform multi-block PLS and optimize the number of components ;; 2. Extract clusters and plot longitudinal profiles ;; 3. Optimize feature selection across all blocks using multi-block sparse PLS ;; 4. Perform post-hoc validation using proportionality distance and Wilcoxon U-tests
workflows.code:
X <- list("X" = profile.filtered, "Z" = timeOmics.simdata$Z)
Y <- as.matrix(timeOmics.simdata$Y)

block.pls.res <- block.pls(X=X, Y=Y, ncomp = 5, 
                           scale = FALSE, mode = "canonical")
block.ncomp <- getNcomp(block.pls.res,X=X, Y=Y, 
                        scale = FALSE, mode = "canonical")
block.pls.res <- block.pls(X=X, Y=Y, ncomp = 1, scale = FALSE, mode = "canonical")
block.pls.cluster <- getCluster(block.pls.res)
plotLong(block.pls.res)
test.list.keepX <- list("X" = 4:10, "Z" = c(2,4,6,8))
test.keepY <- c(2,4,6)

tune.block.res <- tuneCluster.block.spls(X= X, Y= Y, 
                                         test.list.keepX=test.list.keepX, 
                                         test.keepY= test.keepY, 
                                         scale=FALSE, 
                                         mode = "canonical", ncomp = 1)
block.pls.res <- block.spls(X=X, Y=Y, 
                            ncomp = 1, 
                            scale = FALSE, 
                            mode = "canonical", 
                            keepX = tune.block.res$choice.keepX, 
                            keepY = tune.block.res$choice.keepY)

head(getCluster(block.pls.res))
plotLong(block.pls.res)
res <- proportionality(block.pls.res)
head(res$propr.distance)[1:6]
pval.propr <- res$pvalue
knitr::kable(pval.propr)
plot(res)
